Lyubashivka Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Liubashivka, Ukraine

Demolished. Founded in 1830, this cemetery was demolished in the early 20th century and presumably built over after WWII; the editorial office of the 'Hliborob' newspaper now occupies part of the grounds. Jewish population reached about 180 (26%) by 1868, growing to roughly 200 families by the early 20th century; Rabbi Shmuel-Zeev Shechter served the community in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. A 1919 Volunteer Army pogrom drove some Jews to flee to Ivanovka, leaving 50-60 families afterward; population reached 671 by 1939. Wehrmacht occupation in summer 1941 established a ghetto, and about 350 Jews were executed that September.
